sourcedFrom: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") (not printed)
cleanIntro:
This guide follows Rock Island Armory's BBR 3.10 Pistol user's manual (September 2016), which does not name the BBR 3.10 9MM, so check your variant against it. The book is the BBR 3.10 book: its specification table and parts drawing are for the .45 ACP model and it never mentions 9mm, so nothing caliber-specific from it is used here. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it.

Armscor's BBR 3.10 book prints one field strip for this sub-compact 1911. Its recoil assembly is a recoil spring guide carrying two recoil springs and a reverse plug, held captive with a bent paper clip while the assembly comes out of the slide.

steps.title: Know what you are holding
steps.action: This guide follows Rock Island Armory's BBR 3.10 Pistol user's manual (September 2016), which does not name the BBR 3.10 9MM, so check your variant against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it; the book's specification table, parts list and exploded drawing are for the .45 ACP model, so none of them is used here.
steps.prose: The book names the BBR 3.10 on its cover and title page, and the only model it specifies is a .45 ACP pistol: 9mm appears nowhere in it. Its field strip is written for the BBR 3.10 without reference to caliber, and that is what this guide uses. Do not take part numbers, spring specifications or capacities for a 9MM from this book; Armscor itself says a parts order has to name the caliber as well as the part number.
steps.quote: When ordering parts, Iit is necessary to specify the model and the caliber aside from the part number.
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Basic Parts, Notes, p.6

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber checked with the slide back
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction, put your free hand under the magazine and press the magazine catch so it drops into your hand. Then pull the slide back and look into the chamber, because a 1911 will hold a round in the chamber with the magazine gone. Keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time, and do not go on until you have seen an empty chamber.
steps.aside: Place your free hand under the magazine to prevent it from falling and press the magazine catch to release and eject the magazine.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Pull the slide back and check the chamber to ensure that the pistol is unloaded and safe to handle.
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 1, p.9

steps.title: Slide stop pushed out at the disassembly notch
steps.action: Draw the slide back until the lug on the slide stop lines up with the disassembly notch, then push the rounded end of the slide stop pin from the right side of the frame and take the stop out on the left. The notch is the only place it will pass, so if it will not move, the slide has drifted off the notch and forcing it will scar the frame. Hold the slide steady at the notch with your other hand while you push.
steps.aside: Push inward and through the frame to disengage slide stop from slide and frame.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back until the lug on the slide stop is opposite the disassembly notch and push rounded end of pin of slide stop found at right side of the frame.
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 2, p.9

steps.title: Slide run forward off the frame rails
steps.action: Run the slide forward along its rails and off the front of the frame. The barrel and the recoil spring guide assembly leave with it, so support the whole assembly as it comes clear. Work over a bench, because the springs are still inside the slide under load.
steps.quote: Pull the slide forward on its guide rails in the frame, the barrel and the recoil spring guide assembly will come out with it.
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 3, p.9

steps.title: Guide pushed forward until its small hole shows
steps.action: With the slide upside down, push the recoil spring guide forward to compress both recoil springs until the small hole in the guide comes out past the recoil spring reverse plug. You are holding the full force of two springs on the guide at this point. Keep the muzzle end away from your face and do not let the guide slip back.
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring guide forward to compress the recoil springs until the small hole on the recoil spring guide comes out of the recoil spring reverse plug
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 4, p.9

steps.title: Bent paper clip through the hole traps the springs
steps.action: Bend about 5/16 inch of the end of a paper clip to a right angle and push it through the hole you have just exposed. That traps the compressed springs on the guide so the assembly can come out as one piece. Ease off the guide slowly and let the clip take the load before you let go.
steps.quote: Insert a paper clip, with 5/16 inch of its end bent at a 90° angle (Fig.1), into the hole; trapping the spring assembly (Fig.2).
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 5, p.9

steps.title: Trapped recoil spring assembly drawn out to the rear
steps.action: With the clip holding the springs, pull the recoil spring assembly rearward and out of the spring tunnel. Leave the clip in place while the assembly is out, because pulling it releases both springs at once. Note how the reverse plug sits, since Armscor names a wrongly refitted reverse plug as damage its warranty does not cover.
steps.quote: At this point, pull the recoil spring assembly rearward and out of the spring tunnel (Fig.3).
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 6, p.9
steps.warn: Not properly reassembling your RIA Firearm resulting in damage, ie reverse plugs!

steps.title: Barrel link tilted forward, barrel out the front
steps.action: Tilt the barrel link forward and draw the barrel out through the front of the slide. Forward is the only way it clears, because the locking lugs on top of the barrel will not pass back through the slide. The link should swing freely on its pin, and a stiff one is worth noting when you clean.
steps.quote: Tilt the barrel link forward to remove the barrel through the front of the slide.
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 7, p.9

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and the trapped recoil spring assembly are now apart, and that is as far as Armscor's cleaning routine takes the pistol: its basic maintenance starts by taking the barrel and slide assembly off the frame. The firing pin, extractor and frame teardown come next in the same book and belong to a deeper strip, not this one.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel and slide assembly from the frame.
steps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Basic Maintenance of your Pistol, p.11

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out under spring pressure
deepSteps.action: Press the firing pin forward with a punch and hold it there, then push the firing pin stop down and out of the back of the slide. The pin and its spring push against your punch the whole time, so if the punch slips before the stop is clear, the pin leaves the slide on its own. Keep the breech end pointed at the bench, not at you.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin by pressing it with a pin while pushing the firing pin stop downwards at the same time and out of the slide.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 8, p.9

deepSteps.title: Extractor prised out by its groove
deepSteps.action: With the firing pin stop gone, the extractor is free in its tunnel. Get a punch into the groove in its rear face and draw it straight back out of the slide. Twisting it instead of drawing it straight can bend the claw.
deepSteps.quote: Pry the extractor with a pin by its groove out of the slide.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Field Stripping: Disassembly, step 9, p.9

deepSteps.title: Grip panels off
deepSteps.action: Unscrew the grip screws and lift the grip panels off both sides. Use a screwdriver that fits the screw heads properly, because these are small and they mark easily. Keep the screws with their panels.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the grip panels by unscrewing the grip screws with a properly-sized screwdriver to avoid damage on screw heads.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Hammer cocked, thumb safety worked out
deepSteps.action: Cock the hammer first, because the thumb safety only comes out with the hammer back. Hold the thumbpiece firmly and draw it out of the frame slowly, twisting it back and forth as it comes. Pulling it straight and hard can launch the safety lock plunger out of its tube.
deepSteps.quote: Cock the hammer. Hold the thumbpiece of the manual thumb safety firmly and pull it out slowly by twisting it back and forth until it is out of the frame.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Hammer eased down by hand
deepSteps.action: Hold the grip safety in, press the trigger and let the hammer down under your thumb rather than letting it fall. A hammer dropped on an empty frame takes a blow it was never meant to. Keep your thumb on it all the way down.
deepSteps.quote: Carefully lower the hammer by grasping the grip safety and squeezing the trigger while holding on to the hammer to ease it down.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Hammer pin pushed out, hammer and strut removed
deepSteps.action: Use the pivot stud on the thumb safety you just removed as the punch, and push the hammer pin out of the frame. The hammer comes out with its strut still attached. Keep the strut, because the book uses it as the tool for the next two pins.
deepSteps.quote: Using the pivot stud of the manual thumb safety, force the hammer pin out of the frame. The hammer and the hammer strut attached to it can now be removed.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Mainspring housing pin out to the right, housing slid down
deepSteps.action: Push the mainspring housing pin out of the right side of the frame with the end of the hammer strut, then slide the mainspring housing down out of its grooves. The housing carries the mainspring, so it comes out as one assembly. Note which way the pin went, because it goes back the other way.
deepSteps.aside: Remove the mainspring housing assembly down off its grooves in the frame.
deepSteps.quote: Use the end of the hammer strut to push the mainspring housing pin out of the right side of the frame.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Grip safety and sear spring out to the rear
deepSteps.action: With the housing gone, the grip safety and the sear spring come out of the back of the frame. Look at how the sear spring sits before you lift it, because its lower end is caught in a slot at the bottom of the frame and its left-hand leaf has to bear on the sear when it goes back. A spring refitted wrong will not hold the sear.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the grip safety and sear spring rearward from the frame.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Sear pin pushed right to left, sear and disconnector out
deepSteps.action: Use the hammer strut again to push the sear pin out from right to left. The sear and disconnector both ride on that pin and come out of the frame together. Keep them together, because they go back as a pair in one set position.
deepSteps.quote: Use the hammer strut again to push the sear pin from right to left, removing it out of the frame. The sear and disconnector, both mounted on the sear pin can now be removed from the frame.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Magazine release turned a quarter and removed
deepSteps.action: Push the magazine release partly in, then turn the magazine release lock a quarter turn from right to left with a screwdriver that fits it. The release assembly then comes out of the frame. Turning the lock without holding the release in will only chew the slot.
deepSteps.aside: Remove the trigger assembly from its recess cuts in the frame.
deepSteps.quote: Push the magazine release partially and rotate the magazine release lock one quarter turn from right to left with properly
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Plungers and spring pushed out of the plunger tube
deepSteps.action: Push the slide stop plunger, the safety lock plunger and the spring between them out of the back of the plunger tube. They are small and spring-loaded, so cover the tube end with your thumb as they come. This is the last of the frame parts the book removes.
deepSteps.quote: Push the combination slide and safety lock plungers, and the spring between them, out to the rear of the plunger tube.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Mainspring housing taken apart
deepSteps.action: To take the housing apart, press the mainspring down with a punch and push the mainspring cap pin out of its hole. The cap, the mainspring and the housing pin retainer then come out of the housing. Keep the punch on the cap until the pin is clear, because the mainspring is under load. This is where Armscor's teardown ends.
deepSteps.aside: The mainspring cap, mainspring and mainspring housing pin retainer can now be removed from the housing.
deepSteps.quote: The mainspring housing assembly is dismantled by forcing the mainspring down with a punch and push the mainspring cap pin out of its hole in the mainspring housing.
deepSteps.cite: BBR 3.10 PISTOL — USER'S MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Armscor index code "C" (index label "C- Manual - BBR 3.10 Pistol") — Maintenance, Frame Disassembly, p.10

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Scrub the bore and chamber with a bore brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent to remove all lead residue
Wipe the bore and chamber dry with a clean cloth

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Work the breech face over with a solvent-wet old toothbrush to lift powder and primer residue
Clean inside the slide, its locking lugs, and the frame and slide rails
Clean the extractor and the firing pin

cleaning.name: WIPE DOWN & OIL
tasks: Wipe every part and surface clean of solvent with a clean, dry cloth
Apply gun oil to the moving parts straight away
For long storage, use a thicker film of acid-free oil and coat the outside with anti-rust oil or gun grease
Do not store it in leather or anything else that holds moisture

reassembly: To reassemble the pistol, the reverse procedure of disassembly is usually followed.
Put the barrel back in through the front of the slide, then the trapped recoil spring assembly into its tunnel, and take the paper clip out only once the guide is seated.
Mount the barrel and slide assembly to the frame by holding both slide and frame bottom side up.
Barrel link must be tilted to the front as far as it can go and make sure the barrel link pin is flush in its seat.
You can now slide the frame forward into the slide rails.
Refit the slide stop through the frame at the disassembly notch.
If you took the frame apart, follow the book's notes for the sear and disconnector, the sear spring and the mainspring housing before the slide goes back on.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, cycle the slide and confirm it returns fully into battery and the slide stop sits flush. Confirm the thumb safety will only go on with the hammer cocked and that it then blocks the hammer, and that the pistol will not fire unless the grip safety is pressed in. Armscor's own line is to check all functions before loading.
